G-4. GUSTOHIN. alias Mstislavoff, alias General Gudjon,
alias A. Koumoff, alias A. Sigisla, alias,
Kolose, alias K. Arseny.

Aged about 47, height 5' 10", rather stout
dark eyes, dark hair, clean shaven, hard features,
has a distinctly military appearance, is married.
Was formerly Colonel of the General Staff of the
Russian Imperial Army. In 1916 and 1917, was
assistant professor to the Military General Staff in
the Military Academy of Petrograd (Leningrad). In
1918-19 was an officer in General Denikin's Army and
from 1920 has been in the service of the Bolsheviks.
First came to Shanghai from Peking on January 14,
1925, and resided at the Burlington Hotel, where he
registered as a Statistician. From March 4, 1925
to March 18, 1925 was at Nanking for the purpose of
collecting information re the number of troops in
the Shanghai-Nanking Area, and instructing students
and strikers in military training. On June 4, 1925
he was arrested at the Burlington Hotel and eventually
deported from the International Settlement of
Shanghai in August of the same year. After being
deported he visited Tientsin and Peking and in
August 1925, the same month in which he was deported
arrived at Kaifeng where he formed a Russian Mission,
which was attached to Feng Yu-hsiang's army under the
name of Gudjon. Gustohin was made officer in
command. He is also reported to have visited Kalgan
in command of certain "Red" Russian troops after
Kaifeng was evacuated by the Kuomintang troops in

G-4. GUSTOHIN，化名 Mstislavoff，化名 Gudjon 将军，
化名 A. Koumoff，化名 A. Sigisla，化名
Kolose，化名 K. Arseny。

年龄约47岁，身高5英尺10英寸，体格较胖，
黑眼睛，黑发，面部无须，面容冷峻，
具有明显的军人气质，已婚。
曾任俄罗斯帝国陆军总参谋部上校。1916年和1917年，
任彼得格勒（列宁格勒）军事学院总参谋部助理教授。1918-19年
在邓尼金将军军队中任职，自1920年起
为布尔什维克效力。于1925年1月14日
首次从北京抵达上海，入住礼查饭店（Burlington Hotel），登记职业为统计员。1925年3月4日
至1925年3月18日期间，他在南京收集
沪宁地区部队人数的情报，并指导学生
和罢工工人进行军事训练。1925年6月4日，
他在礼查饭店被捕，并于同年8月最终
被驱逐出上海公共租界。被驱逐后，他访问了天津和北京，并于1925年8月，即他被驱逐的同一个月，
抵达开封，在那里组建了一个俄罗斯代表团，
以 Gudjon 的名义隶属于冯玉祥的军队。Gustohin 被任命
为指挥官。另有报告称，在1926年6月国民党军队撤离开封后，
他曾指挥某些“红色”俄罗斯部队访问张家口，

page_data.en:
- 2 -

June 1926, and to have maintained a Russian detachment
for Wu Pei Fu at Loyang, for which men were recruited
secretly from Shanghai. Visited Shanghai in April, 1927
when he was reported to have been appointed a military
adviser to Chinag Kai-shek, but owing to the latter's
change of policy towards the communists, returned to
Hankow in May, 1927, and became a military instructor
to the Hankow Government. During the following days he
seems to have been somewhat elusive and on June 23,
1927 he suddenly arrived in Shanghai from Canton under
the name of A. Koumoff and lived in the Plaza Hotel.
On the following day, June 24, he disappeared again and
returned to Shanghai from Nanking on July 13, travell-
ing under the name of Koloso. It was also reported
that he arrived in Nanking from Hankow on the evening of
July 10 and 11. On the occasion of the latter visit he
stated that he had been appointed Senior Adviser at
General Chiang Kai-shek's Headquarters. He is still
residing at the Plaza Hotel. For some time during
1925 he was Military Adviser to the Soviet consulate
in Shanghai.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

并在洛阳为吴佩孚维持一支俄罗斯分遣队，为此他在上海秘密招募人员。1927年4月访问上海，
据报道他被任命为蒋介石的军事顾问，但由于后者
对共产党政策的改变，他于1927年5月返回汉口，
并成为汉口政府的军事教官。在接下来的日子里，
他的行踪似乎有些飘忽不定，1927年6月23日，
他突然以 A. Koumoff 的名字从广州抵达上海，住在华懋公寓（Plaza Hotel）。
次日，即6月24日，他再次失踪，并于7月13日从南京返回上海，
使用 Koloso 的名字旅行。另有报告称，
他于7月10日和11日晚从汉口抵达南京。在后一次访问期间，
他声称已被任命为蒋介石将军总部的高级顾问。他目前
仍居住在华懋公寓。在1925年的一段时间里，他曾担任苏联驻上海领事馆的军事顾问。

July 15, 1927.
REPORT ON Soviet General Gustchin, alias Mstislavoff, alias
General Gudjon, alias A. Koumoff, alias A. Sigiflis.
Made by D.S.I. Robertson. Forwarded by J. Kinners C. D. I.
Sir,
The foreigner named Kolose, Senior Adviser at
General Chiang Kai Shek's Military Headquarters, who is mentioned
in the Intelligence Report of July 13 as having arrived at
Shanghai North Station from Nanking at 7.15 a.m. July 13, is
the notorious General Gustchin, who is now staying at the Plaza
Hotel Room 314 under the name of K. Arseny.
It is reported that Gustchin arrived from Hankow
at Nanking on the "Tafoo Maru" on the night of July 10-11 and
after interviewing General Chiang Kai Shek came here to recuperate.
Since his arrival in Shanghai he has renewed
his acquaintance with his paramour Mrs. De Sheimo and frequently
visits her at 390 Avenue Joffre.
I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
A. Robertson
D. S. I.
（批：His Staff Officer denies that any Russians are employed by the General）
D.C.I. (Copy to Capt. Shelley Ops. 7.2)

July 2, 1927

REPORT ON Soviet General Gustchin, alias Matislavoff, alias
General Gudjon, alias A. Koumoff, alias A. Sigidis.

Made by P.C.S. Kedrolivansky Forwarded by Robertson, D.S.I.

Sir,

I beg to report that a notorious Soviet Military
agent in China, named A. Gustchin, arrived here from Canton
on June 23, 1927 by the s.s. "President Taft" under the name
of A. Koumoff. He was accompanied by his aide-de-camp
W. Mouravieff.

On their arrival in Shanghai they proceeded to
the "Hotel de France" where they registered as Mr. A. Sigidis
and W. Mouravieff respectively.

On June 24 they left the Hotel and W. Mouravieff
went to No. 220 Rue Chapsal, where he is at present residing.

No trace of Gustchin has been found since he
left the Hotel, but it is reported that he went to Hankow under
an assumed name.

The paramour of Gustchin, Mrs. De Sheimo is now
living at No. 390 Avenue Joffre. Her movements are being
watched in an endeavour to locate the whereabouts of Gustchin.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant.
V. Kedrolivansky
P. C. S.

D. C. I.

关于苏联将军 Gustchin，化名 Matislavoff，化名
Gudjon 将军，化名 A. Koumoff，化名 A. Sigidis 的报告。

由 P.C.S. Kedrolivansky 制作，由 D.S.I. Robertson 转呈。

先生，

谨此报告，一名在中国活动的臭名昭著的苏联军事
特工，名为 A. Gustchin，于1927年6月23日
以 A. Koumoff 之名乘“塔夫脱总统”号轮船从广州抵达此处。陪同他的是其副官
W. Mouravieff。

抵达上海后，他们前往“法兰西酒店”（Hotel de France），分别登记为 A. Sigidis 先生
和 W. Mouravieff。

6月24日，他们离开酒店，W. Mouravieff
前往霞裴尔路220号，他目前居住于此。

自 Gustchin 离开酒店后，未发现其踪迹，但有报告称他以假名前往汉口。

Gustchin 的情妇 De Sheimo 夫人现居
霞飞路390号。正在监视她的行踪，以期确定 Gustchin 的下落。

先生，
您顺从的仆人。
V. Kedrolivansky
P. C. S.

D. C. I.

June, 4 192 5

REPORT ON Interrogation of a Suspected Bolshevik Agent.

Made by D. S. Korolkoff, 31 Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

I beg to report that today, on June 4, I acted as interpreter at the Louza Station when Mr Maitland, Police Solicitor, questioned a Russian arrested at the Burlington Hotel this morning.

The man admitted that his name is Alexander Gushchin, Russian General Staff, Colonel through Imperial promotion., who in 1916 and 1917 was an assistant professor at the General Staff Military Academy at Petrograd.

He admitted also that since his arrival in Shanghai, in January, 1925, he has been staying at the Burlington Hotel under the name of Mstislavoff, but said that he never used the pseudonyms of Mstislavsky or Vyacheslavsky. Gushchin denied that he turned over to the Bolsheviks after the Bolshevist Revolution stating that during 1918 and 1919 he was fighting against the Reds in General Denikin's Army and was then evacuated to Constantinople. He states that he well knows Gecker, Military Attache to Karahan, as Gecker was amongst his students in the Academy. Gushchin-Mstislavoff denies that he brought with him a large sum of money from Russia and says that he brought only about 900 gold dollars, his own property, and that this has been nearly spent here. He is willing to leave Shanghai for Russia. He has only about 300 dollars Mex. on him. Gushchin says that he is not a Communist nor an Internationalist, but he is a "neutral", one of the many in Russia now, who are in the service of the Bolsheviks at present and who long for "another Russia". He is a Soviet subject and produced a Soviet passport issued by the local Red Consulate.

1925年6月4日

关于审讯一名疑似布尔什维克特工的报告。

由 D. S. Korolkoff, 31 制作，由 [签名] 转呈

先生，

谨此报告，今日，即6月4日，我在老闸巡捕房担任翻译，当时警务律师 Maitland 先生讯问了一名今晨在礼查饭店被捕的俄罗斯人。

该男子承认其名为 Alexander Gushchin，系俄罗斯总参谋部上校（经帝国晋升），1916年和1917年曾任彼得格勒总参谋部军事学院助理教授。

他还承认，自1925年1月抵达上海以来，他一直以 Mstislavoff 之名住在礼查饭店，但称他从未使用过 Mstislavsky 或 Vyacheslavsky 等化名。Gushchin 否认在布尔什维克革命后投奔布尔什维克，声称在1918年和1919年期间，他在邓尼金将军的军队中与红军作战，随后撤至君士坦丁堡。他表示非常认识 Karahan 的武官 Gecker，因为 Gecker 曾是他在学院的学生。Gushchin-Mstislavoff 否认从俄罗斯携带大量资金，称他只带了约900金元，属其个人财产，且在此地已几乎花光。他愿意离开上海前往俄罗斯。他身上仅有约300墨西哥元。Gushchin 称他不是共产主义者也不是国际主义者，而是一个“中立者”，是俄罗斯目前众多为布尔什维克服务并渴望“另一个俄罗斯”的人之一。他是苏维埃公民，并出示了当地红色领事馆签发的苏维埃护照。

He emphatically denies any connection with the Red Consulate
to which place, he says, he has been once and that was to change his
passport. Gushchin says that he knows neither Ozornin nor Wilde.
He admits that he was making enquiries with the local Whites
and anti-Bolshevik organizations, but no explanation was given by him
Questioned about his teaching Chinese Students as a Military
Instructor he said that he does not even know a man amongst
the Chinese.
He produced tickets to go to Peking en route for Russia
this night and explained that his sudden departure is due to the
note in yesterday's copy of the Russia" accusing him of being
the Military Instructor of the rioters. This was forcing him
to leave Shanghai as soon as possible as "he has no means to
defend himself".
Mr Maitland consented to let him leave Shanghai this night
instead of having to appear before the Court to-morrow on a charge
of being an undesirable, but warned him to abstain from returning
to Shanghai.
Gushchin is being detained at the Louza Station until his
departure and D.S. Papp has been charged with conveying him to
the S. N. R. Station and to ascertain the hour of his departure.

I am, Sir,
your obedient servant
B. Horolkoff
D. S. 81.

D. C. I.
Noted.
JMS

他坚决否认与红色领事馆有任何联系，

当被问及作为军事教官教导中国学生时，

June 4, 1925.

REPORT ON Guschin-Mstislavoff alias Mstislavsky or Vyacheslavsky.

Made by T.P.O.O. Kedrolivansky Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

A Russian, who resides at Burlington Hotel under the name of Mr. Mstislavoff, is actually Guschin, Soviet Military Agent in Shanghai. It is stated also that he may appear sometimes under the names of Mstislavsky or Vyacheslavsky. It is known that Guschin-Mstislavoff, then a Colonel of the Russian Imperial General Staff, was, at the time of the March Revolution in 1917, an assistant-professor at the General-Staff Military Academy in Petrograd, and afterwards went over to the Bolsheviks. He is a personal friend of Mr. Gecker, Military Attaché to Karahan.

Guschin-Mstislavoff came here from Peking in January 1925 and was staying at the Burlington Hotel, room No. 69, showing his profession to be a "Statistician". He speaks French perfectly. a little German and very little English. He is alleged to have brought large funds here and to have special secret instructions. It is stated that his principal task is the collecting of information regarding the allocation of Chinese troops in Kiangsu Province and their movements. With the same purpose Mstislavoff left Shanghai for Nanking on March 4, 1925 and came back on March 18. He is residing at the Burlington Hotel. It is stated also that besides his principal duties of a Military Agent, he has been instructed to keep a watch over the local "White" officers and take steps to persuade them to return to Russia.

Guschin-Mstislavoff often meets Kister-Ozornin, Soviet Consul General here, and Wilde, Soviet Vice Consul.

D. U. I.
I am, Sir,
Your Obedient servant,
V. Kedrolivansky
T. P. O. O.

关于 Guschin-Mstislavoff，化名 Mstislavsky 或 Vyacheslavsky 的报告。

由 T.P.O.O. Kedrolivansky 制作，由 [签名] 转呈

先生，

一名以 Mstislavoff 先生之名居住在礼查饭店的俄罗斯人，实为 Guschin，系在上海的苏联军事特工。据说他有时也以 Mstislavsky 或 Vyacheslavsky 的名字出现。众所周知，Guschin-Mstislavoff 时任俄罗斯帝国总参谋部上校，在1917年三月革命期间，是彼得格勒总参谋部军事学院的助理教授，后来投奔布尔什维克。他是 Karahan 的武官 Gecker 先生的私人朋友。

Guschin-Mstislavoff 于1925年1月从北京来到此处，住在礼查饭店69号房间，申报职业为“统计员”。他能说流利的法语，略懂德语，英语很差。据称他携带大量资金来此，并持有特殊的秘密指令。据说他的主要任务是收集关于江苏省中国军队部署及其调动的情报。出于同样目的，Mstislavoff 于1925年3月4日离开上海前往南京，并于3月18日返回。他居住在礼查饭店。另据称，除了作为军事特工的主要职责外，他还受命监视当地的“白俄”军官，并采取措施说服他们返回俄罗斯。

Guschin-Mstislavoff 经常与此处的苏联总领事 Kister-Ozornin 和苏联副领事 Wilde 会面。

D. U. I.
先生，
您顺从的仆人，
V. Kedrolivansky
T. P. O. O.

3.6.1925.
"Russia" reports the following:- Great nervousness
is observed amongst the Soviet leaders. A rumour is in
circulation to the effect that the Soviet Consulate has
sent a radio to Moscow asking for instructions and money
for the development of this movement.
It has been ascertained that after the scandalous
revelation of the Sunday meeting at the Soviet Consulate,
the Headquarters of the strike have been transferred to the
Chinese Students' Union, Chapei.
Mysterious and disguised messengers are constantly
running from the Headquarters to the Soviet Consulate
with "reports".
It has been confirmed that an organization of a Sovdep
(Council of the Labour and Soldier Deputies) and of the
Red Guards is being carried on in Chapei under the
direction of Soviet agents.
The agents of the Chinese Students' Union, members of
the Koumingtang party and members of the Chinese Volunteer
Corps are acting jointly, and in accordance with the
instructions of the Soviet Consulate. Gusohin-Mstislavoff,
of the Russian General Staff, who used to live at the
Burlington Hotel is their Military Instructor.

1925年6月3日。
“俄罗斯”方面报告如下：苏联领导人中观察到极大的紧张情绪。有谣言流传，称苏联领事馆已向莫斯科发送无线电报，请求指示及资金以发展此运动。
经查实，在苏联领事馆周日集会丑闻曝光后，罢工总部已迁至闸北的中国学生联合会。
神秘且伪装的信使不断从总部携带“报告”往返于苏联领事馆。
已证实，在苏联特工的指导下，闸北正在组建苏维埃（工农兵代表会议）及赤卫队组织。
中国学生联合会的代理人、国民党党员以及中华志愿团成员正协同行动，并遵照苏联领事馆的指示行事。前居百老汇路礼查饭店（Burlington Hotel）的俄军总参谋部古索欣-姆斯季斯拉夫（Gusohin-Mstislavoff）是他们的军事教官。

FurtherREPORT ON Riots in Louza District.
Made by D.S. Douglas Forwarded by [签名]
Sir,
I beg to report that everything has been quiet for the past 24 hours.
At 8.15 a.m. on the 4/6/25 I arrested a Russian Known General Guschin at the Burlington Hotel. a Russian woman who had spent the night with him was also arrested but subsequently released.
General Guschin was interrogated by Mr Maitland (P.S.) and he decided that he should be escorted to the train which leaves Shanghai at 11 p.m. this inst. (4/6/25) as he has Railway tickets in his possession, covering transportation from Shanghai to Peking. He states that he is a Bolshevist but not a Communit and denies taking any part in the present trouble and states that he will not return to Shanghai.
Information has been received by me on at least four occasions, so I communicated with the D.C.I. suggesting that the rooms of this man (General Guschin) be searched, and the man arrested.
Authority was granted by the D.C.I. and together with Special Police I went to the Burlington Hotel and arrested the said man.
He will be escorted to the train and seen off by Foreign detectives.
A further report will follow on subsequent developments.
I am, Sir,
Your Obedient Servant
[签名]
Det. Sergt.
（批：Noted [签名]）
D. C. I.

1925年6月4日
关于老闸区骚乱的补充报告。
由 D.S. Douglas 呈报 [签名]

先生，
谨此报告，过去24小时内一切平静。
1925年6月4日上午8时15分，我在礼查饭店逮捕了一名被称为古申（Guschin）将军的俄国人。一名与他共度夜晚的俄国女子也被逮捕，但随后获释。
梅特兰先生（警务副总监）对古申将军进行了审讯，并决定将其押送至今晚11时离开上海的列车，因为他持有从上海至北京的车票。他自称是布尔什维克，但不是共产主义者，否认参与当前的骚乱，并表示不会返回上海。
我至少四次收到有关此人的情报，因此我与刑事调查主任联系，建议搜查此人（古申将军）的房间并将其逮捕。
刑事调查主任批准了该请求，我与特别警察一同前往礼查饭店，逮捕了上述男子。
他将被押送至火车站，并由外籍侦探送行。
后续进展将另行报告。
先生，
您忠实的仆人
[签名]
警佐

刑事调查主任

关于布尔什维克行动的注释
在天津
将审议一名臭名昭著的布尔什维克特工的案件。
上校古申（Gushin）此前在礼查饭店被捕并被驱逐至北方。据悉，他在天津被枪决。
古申当时正在华界参加布尔什维克短期政治委员会的一次会议，该地点遭到张作霖元帅士兵的突袭。布尔什维克分子发现被困后开火，天津士兵随即还击，古申与十名中国人被枪杀。
